personas.label: Marketing analytics professionals
personas.description: You report on campaign and media performance and want to prove you can set up Marketing Cloud Intelligence well.

personas.label: Data-driven marketing consultants
personas.description: You help clients pull marketing data from many platforms into one place.

personas.label: BI specialists moving into marketing analytics

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Marketing Cloud Intelligence Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: It is a moderate exam. The hardest part is the data side: bringing in data from many platforms, mapping it to the data model and making the numbers add up correctly. Dashboard questions are usually easier.
bullets: About 65% to pass, roughly 39 correct answers. Check the official guide for the current figure.
Data focus. Data streams, mapping, harmonisation and how measurements are aggregated.
Reporting. Dashboards, widgets, filters and calculated measurements.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: People who have connected several ad platforms and built a cross-channel dashboard do best. Before you book. Aim for 75% or more on practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Marketing Cloud Intelligence Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions describe a data problem, such as the same campaign named differently on two platforms or totals that look too high, and ask how to fix it.
bestWayToPass: Learn data streams: How data comes in through connectors or files, and how often.
Understand mapping: Each source field is mapped to a dimension or measurement in the data model.
Master harmonisation: Making data from different platforms line up, for example by a shared campaign key.
Know aggregation: Why some measures should be summed and others should not.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you set up Marketing Cloud Intelligence: bringing in marketing data, mapping and harmonising it, building calculated measures, and creating dashboards.

keyConcepts.h2: Marketing Cloud Intelligence: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Intelligence Platform Architecture
blocks.body: Marketing Cloud Intelligence brings marketing data from many sources, such as ad platforms, web analytics, email and CRM, into one place for reporting. Data is organised in **workspaces**, which can hold different brands or clients. Inside, a shared **data model** gives every source the same structure, with **dimensions** (things you describe, like campaign, channel or date) and **measurements** (things you count, like spend, clicks or conversions). Once data fits the model, it can be compared across channels in one dashboard.

blocks.heading: Data Streams and Harmonisation
blocks.body: Each source comes in through a **data stream**, using a built-in connector or a file upload. During setup you **map** each source field to a dimension or measurement in the model. **Harmonisation** makes data from different sources line up. For example, if Google Ads and Meta use different campaign names, you can use a shared key or naming pattern so both link to the same campaign. Classification rules can create new dimensions from patterns in names, such as reading the product line from a campaign name.

blocks.heading: Insights, KPIs, and Custom Metrics
blocks.body: Beyond raw data, teams need numbers like cost per acquisition or return on ad spend. **Calculated measurements** are formulas built from other measurements. **Calculated dimensions** group or relabel values. **Aggregation** matters: spend and clicks can be added up, but rates like click-through rate must be recalculated from their parts, not summed. Getting aggregation wrong is a common reason totals look strange. Insights features can flag unusual changes in key numbers.

blocks.heading: Dashboards and Data Visualisation
blocks.body: **Dashboards** are made of pages and **widgets**, such as charts, tables and single-number tiles. **Filters** let users narrow by date, channel or campaign. Good dashboards start with the question the viewer needs answered and show only what helps answer it. Share dashboards with the right users, and schedule them to be emailed if people need regular updates. Pivot-style tables help analysts explore data before deciding what goes on a dashboard.

blocks.heading: API Integration and Automation
blocks.body: Data streams can run on a **schedule**, so dashboards stay current without manual uploads. When a built-in connector doesn't exist, data can be sent through files or APIs. Marketing Cloud Intelligence data can also be shared with other tools, such as Salesforce or a data warehouse. Monitor data stream runs and set alerts so failed loads are noticed quickly, since a missed load leaves gaps in reports.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Marketing Cloud Intelligence Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions start with a data problem. Ask whether it comes from how data was brought in, how it was mapped, or how it is being added up.

blocks.heading: Data Streams & Connectors
blocks.body: Use built-in connectors where possible. Set a schedule so data stays current.

blocks.heading: Data Model & Harmonization
blocks.body: Map every field to the right dimension or measurement. Use shared keys to link the same campaign across sources.

blocks.heading: Model Builder
blocks.body: Build calculated measurements for KPIs like cost per acquisition. Recalculate rates from their parts.

blocks.heading: Dashboard Design
blocks.body: Start from the viewer's question. Use filters instead of building many near-identical pages.

blocks.heading: Einstein Integration
blocks.body: Use automated insights to spot sudden changes in performance that need attention.

sampleQuestions.question: The same campaign appears as 'Spring_Sale_US' in Google Ads and 'US Spring Sale' in Meta. The team wants one combined row. What should be done?
options: Harmonise the sources with a shared campaign key or naming pattern
Rename each one of the campaigns by hand at the end of every single week
Report on each platform separately
Delete one of the data streams
sampleQuestions.explanation: Harmonisation links data from different sources to the same campaign, so it can be combined.
whyWrong: Manual renaming is slow and breaks easily.
Separate reports don't give the combined view.
Deleting a stream loses data.

sampleQuestions.question: A dashboard shows click-through rate summed across campaigns, giving 340%. What is wrong?
options: There are too many widgets
The rate is being summed instead of recalculated from clicks and impressions
The data stream is late
The filter has been applied to entirely the wrong date field on the dashboard
sampleQuestions.explanation: Rates must be calculated from their parts after adding up clicks and impressions, not summed directly.
whyWrong: Widget count doesn't affect the maths.
Late data wouldn't create a rate over 100%.
Date filters don't cause summed rates.

sampleQuestions.question: When setting up a new data stream, what must be done with each source field?
options: Map it to a dimension or measurement
Leave it unmapped
Add it to a dashboard first
Rename the field in the original source system instead
sampleQuestions.explanation: Mapping puts each field in the right place in the shared model, so it can be used and compared.
whyWrong: Unmapped fields can't be used in reports.
Data must be mapped before it can be shown.
Source names don't need changing.

sampleQuestions.question: Which of these is a measurement rather than a dimension?
options: Spend
Campaign name
Country
Channel
sampleQuestions.explanation: Measurements are numbers you add up or calculate, like spend. Dimensions describe the data, like campaign or channel.
whyWrong: Campaign name is a dimension.
Country is a dimension.
Channel is a dimension.

sampleQuestions.question: The team needs cost per acquisition for each channel. What should they create?
options: A new data stream configured for that advertising platform
A calculated measurement of spend divided by conversions
A filter
A new workspace
sampleQuestions.explanation: Calculated measurements build KPIs from existing measurements.
whyWrong: A new stream brings in data, it doesn't calculate KPIs.
Filters narrow data, they don't create measures.
A workspace organises data, it doesn't calculate.

sampleQuestions.question: Campaign names follow a pattern like 'BRAND_PRODUCT_COUNTRY'. The team wants a Product dimension. What should they use?
options: Ask each of the teams to add a product field to their own files
A new workspace
Create a dashboard filter
A classification rule that extracts the product from the name
sampleQuestions.explanation: Rules can read values from naming patterns and create new dimensions automatically.
whyWrong: Adding fields everywhere is slow and needs every platform to change.
A workspace doesn't create dimensions.
A filter can't create a dimension.

sampleQuestions.question: Dashboards are out of date because someone forgot to upload last week's file. What should be changed?
options: Add more widgets
Upload the source files a good deal less often
Schedule the data stream to run automatically
Delete the dashboard
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scheduled data streams keep data current without relying on manual uploads.
whyWrong: Widgets don't load data.
Less often makes it worse.
Deleting the dashboard doesn't fix the data.

sampleQuestions.question: An agency manages marketing data for three separate clients who must not see each other's data. How should this be organised?
options: Separate widgets for each client
One single dashboard with a client filter applied
One data stream for all clients
Separate workspaces for each client
sampleQuestions.explanation: Workspaces keep each client's data and setup separate.
whyWrong: Widgets don't separate access.
A filter doesn't stop people seeing other clients' data.
One stream mixes all the data.

sampleQuestions.question: A data stream failed overnight and nobody noticed for a week. What should be set up?
options: A new KPI
More filters
A single larger dashboard layout
Monitoring and alerts on the runs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Alerts on failed runs let the team fix problems before reports are affected.
whyWrong: A KPI doesn't monitor loads.
Filters don't detect failures.
Dashboard size doesn't detect failures.

sampleQuestions.question: A dashboard viewer only wants to see last month's results for the email channel. What should they use?
options: A new data stream configured for that advertising platform
A newly created calculated measurement
Filters for date and channel
A new workspace
sampleQuestions.explanation: Filters let users narrow the dashboard without changing the data or building new pages.
whyWrong: A new stream isn't needed to view existing data.
A calculated measurement creates a new number, it doesn't narrow data.
A workspace is far more than needed.

sampleQuestions.question: A connector doesn't exist for a small ad platform the client uses. How can its data be brought in?
options: By copying it into a widget
Through a file upload or API data stream
It can't be used
By typing the value directly into a dashboard widget
sampleQuestions.explanation: File and API-based streams can bring in data from sources without a built-in connector.
whyWrong: Widgets display data.
Data can still be brought in another way.
Dashboards display data, they don't store it.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the main reason to bring all marketing data into one data model?
options: So results can be compared across channels and platforms
So that each platform's own reports continue to look different
So dashboards load more slowly
So data stays in separate tools
sampleQuestions.explanation: A shared model makes data from different sources comparable in one place.
whyWrong: The aim is consistency, not difference.
Speed isn't the reason.
Keeping data separate defeats the purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: Total conversions look doubled after adding a second data stream that also reports conversions. What is the likely cause?
options: The workspace is too small
The dashboard simply has a great many more pages than it needs
The same conversions are counted in both sources and need de-duplicating
The filter is wrong
sampleQuestions.explanation: When two sources report the same events, adding them together double-counts. Decide which source to trust or de-duplicate.
whyWrong: Workspace size isn't a factor.
Page count doesn't double numbers.
A filter wouldn't double the total.

sampleQuestions.question: Leaders want an automatic heads-up when cost per click jumps unexpectedly. What helps?
options: Removing the KPI
Adding more data streams
Automated insights or alerts on that KPI
Checking the dashboard over just once every quarter
sampleQuestions.explanation: Insights and alerts flag unusual changes so the team can act quickly.
whyWrong: Removing the KPI hides the problem.
More streams don't spot changes.
Quarterly checks are too slow.

sampleQuestions.question: What should a well-designed dashboard start from?
options: The colour scheme
The question the viewer must answer
Every available widget
Whichever is the largest data stream
sampleQuestions.explanation: Good dashboards are built around the decisions viewers need to make.
whyWrong: Colours come after content.
Too many widgets make dashboards hard to read.
Data size doesn't decide what to show.
